elements.evidence: Section 6.1 prohibits the Company from participating in similar Internet projects involving Deerskin Products and grants HDI an exclusive right concerning the Deerskin-branded consumer website.
Although not labeled a sole-supplier obligation, HDI's exclusive right prevents the Company from using an alternative provider for the covered Deerskin-branded website during the exclusivity period.

elements.element: Any exclusivity binding Customer is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The redline confines the restriction to the specific, capitalized category “Deerskin Products” and deletes the broader references to substantially similar products and similar companies.

elements.element: Any exclusivity binding Customer lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 applies only “during the 12 months following the Effective Date,” notwithstanding the Agreement's automatic renewals.

elements.element: Customer's exclusivity obligations terminate automatically if Vendor fails to meet a service level.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence states that the Company's Section 6.1 obligations “shall terminate automatically upon HDI's failure to meet any service level.”

elements.element: Customer's exclusivity obligations terminate automatically if Vendor fails to meet a delivery date.
elements.evidence: The same sentence expressly provides automatic termination upon HDI's failure to meet “any ... delivery date.”

result.reason: The redline retains exclusivity binding the Company, so it does not satisfy the preferred position. It does satisfy the fallback by narrowing the scope to Deerskin Products, limiting the restriction to 12 months from the Effective Date, and automatically terminating the Company's Section 6.1 obligations upon either specified Vendor performance failure. The changes are confined to those fallback requirements and do not disturb the Agreement's general term or renewal provisions.
